CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI) Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent No.2 - insurance company.
02.

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed in MVC.809/2018 dated 31.03.2021, by the learned I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.

The factual matrix of the case are that on 12.03.2018, the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-39-L-9535, a Cruiser bearing Reg.No.KA-35-M- 6432, came from opposite direction and collided with the petitioner, resulting in injuries to him.
In the said accident, he suffered multiple injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to hospital Chitguppa and then to higher facility at Bidar.
He was in patient from 12.03.2018 to 17.03.2018.

He contended that he was aged of Shaik Mohammed vs Revansidh And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19523587/
2 38 years and was an electrician and tent worker and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

sentences.text: He had approached the Tribunal seeking compensation.
04. On being served with the notice, the respondents appeared, but respondent No.2 alone filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company contested the petition contending that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable.
It denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner.
It was contended that there were violation of the terms and conditions of the policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, it repudiated its liability to pay any compensation.

The Tribunal framed appropriate issues and the petitioner was examined as PW.1 and two doctors who assessed the disability were examined PW.2 and PW.3 and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 were marked in the evidence.

No evidence was led on behalf of the respondents.
06.

After hearing both sides, the Tribunal awarded the compensation of Rs.4,53,700/- under the following heads:-
 Sl. Heads Compensation  No. Awarded  1. Pain and suffering Rs.15,000/-
 2. Attendant charges, food and Rs.3,000/-
 conveyance charges

3 . Loss of future income Rs.3,38,400/-
 4. Medical expenditure Rs.75,500/-
5. Loss of income during treatment Rs.11,800/-
Loss of amenities and nutrition 6. Rs.10,000/-
food

Total compensation Rs.4,53,700/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:902 07.

While coming to the conclusion the Tribunal held that there is 16% disability to the petitioner and in the absence of any proof of income, notional income of Rs.11,750/- was adopted and holding that he was aged 38 years, multiplier of 15 was adopted by it.
08. Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.
09. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that there were 07 fractures, loss of 06 teeth.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- only under the head of pain and Shaik Mohammed vs Revansidh And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19523587/
3 suffering.

sentences.text: It is contended that several visits to the hospital for the purpose of fixing of the dentures were also not considered and the cost of the denture and implants and removal of the implants as stated by PW.2 and PW.3 is not at all considered by the Tribunal.
It is submitted that the functional disability of the petitioner has not been properly appreciated by the Tribunal.
It is pointed out that though PW.2 had stated that there is a disability of 48%.

The Tribunal without NC:
2025:KHC-K:902 applying its mind as to what extent it will translate into functional disability, has adopted the standard of taking 1/3rd of the physical disability as a functional disability.

Therefore,
he contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
10. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 - insurance company would contend that the Tribunal is justified in taking the disability at 16%.

When the petitioner had not placed any material to show his avocation, he contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the remaining heads is also adequate and no indulgence required by this Court.
It is pointed out that only 02 teeth have been lost.
The enhancement claimed is not justifiable.

11. A perusal of the records would disclose as per Ex.P.6 - wound certificate, Ex.P.7 - discharge summary and Ex.P.9 - disability certificate, the petitioner had sustained the following injuries:-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:902 1. Fracture of the bilateral anterior medial and posterior walls of maxillary sinuses and hemo sinuses.
2. Fracture of lateral wall of left orbit.
3. Fracture of boney nasal septum.
4. ACLW on the lips.
5. Fracture of both the bones of the right forearm open wound on the right leg.
6. Fracture of lower limb of 1/3rd of the right fibula.
12.
These documents also show that the fractures were treated with a ORIF and LCP plating etc., and wound debridement was done.
He was inpatient for 5 days.
13. The PW.2 who has issued the disability certificate states that there were fracture of both the bones of the right forearm.
Fracture of the right lower 3rd of the fibula.
These fractures contribute much to the disability.
According to him, there is a disability of 48%, out of which 30% is attributed to the upper limb and 40% NC: 2025:KHC-K:902 to the lower limb.
He has opined that the fractures are malunited.
The PW.3, who is a dentist, has issued the disability certificate as per Ex.P.9; has noted that there was fracture of the maxillary sinus, fracture of the orbital fracture of the nasal septum.
The petitioner had lost 02 teeth.
There were fractures of 03 teeth.
Ultimately, he opined that there is a difficulty for the petitioner for mastication.

He opined that replacing the Shaik Mohammed vs Revansidh And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19523587/
4 missing teeth and treatment of the fractured teeth would involve a cost of Rs.1,56,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He opines that there is a need for RCT of the fractured teeth fixing of the crown etc.
PW.2 also stated that there is a need for about Rs.80,000/- for removal of the implants.
14. When we examine the above injuries suffered by the petitioner, it is evident that he being a manual worker; being a tent worker or an electrician, it requires movement.
Obviously, the petitioner has suffered fractures of both bones of the dominant hand.
Evidently, that would cause difficulty to use his right hand and he is a electrician.

The fracture of the fibula is also an injury, NC:
2025:KHC-K:902 which would cause hindrance in movement.

Therefore, when PW.2 has observed that functional the physical disability at 40% and 30% and opines that the whole body disability is 48%, it was required by the Tribunal that it should have dealt with the assessment of the functional disability.
15. The Tribunal without discussing anything has held that 1/3rd of the whole body disability is to be taken as the functional disability.

The judgment of Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar1, as well as Sidram vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and Another2, laid down that assessing the functional disability is to be done by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Sidram vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical experts can only say about the physical disability, but they cannot opine in respect of the functional disability.

In that view of the matter, considering the avocation of the petitioner and the nature of the injuries suffered by him, this Court is of the opinion that the functional disability has to be taken at 25%.
It is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has not at all awarded any compensation in respect of the future medical expenses.
There were fractures to the maxillary sinus and he had lost two teeth and other four teeth had suffered fractures.
There was requirement of RCT crowning, etc., this aspect was never considered by the Tribunal in assessing the compensation.

In the considered opinion of this court, for removal of the implants, it would be proper to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- and to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- in respect of the cost of the dentures and such related expenses.
In all the petitioner is entitled for future medical expenses at Rs.1,00,000/-.
17. The petitioner being aged 39 years is not in dispute.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier would be '15'.

The Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.11,750/- which is in consonance with the notional income prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalath.

In umpteen number of judgments, this Court has - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:902 held that the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of disputes before Lok-Adalath regarding notional income is in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.

Therefore, the loss of future Shaik Mohammed vs Revansidh And Anr on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19523587/
5 income on account of disability is calculated as Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 15 x 25% = Rs.5,28,750/-
18.

sentences.text: Consequently, the loss of income during the laid up period has to be assessed for a period of 3 months and therefore, a sum of Rs.35,250/- has to be awarded under this head.
19. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.

In the considered opinion of this court, the same has to be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-
20.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head of loss of amenities in life.
It is relevant to note from the discomfort of fracture of the nasal bone and orbit and the loss of teeth, it is going to haunt the petitioner for the rest of his life.

Though, this injury has - 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:902 not contributed for the functional disability, the discomfort on account of use of dentures or crowning and such related injuries has to be accounted for, therefore, the compensation under the head of loss of amenities is to be enhanced to Rs.75,000/-.

21. Considering the multiple injuries suffered by the petitioner and his requirement to visit dentist as well as the regular hospital, the conveyance expenses, attendant charges, etc., is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
22. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the remaining heads does not call for any interference by this Court.

23. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Attendant charges, Food and Rs.10,000/-
Conveyance charges Loss of future income Rs.5,28,750/-
Medical expenditure Rs.1,00,000/-
Loss of income during the laid up Rs.35,250/-
period Loss of amenities Rs.75,000/-
Total Rs.7,99,000/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.4,53,700/-
Enhancement Rs.3,45,300/-

6 24.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,45,300/- with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.3,45,300/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
iii. Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
The other conditions in respect of the deposit, etc., remain unaltered.
